name: CI

on:
  push:
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:

jobs:
  # Deterministic regression test for issue #3. The Playwright browser bundle's
  # Chrome directory name is NOT stable across versions:
  #   playwright-driver 1.56.1 -> chromium-1194/chrome-linux/chrome   (no `64`)
  #   playwright-driver 1.60.0 -> chromium-1223/chrome-linux64/chrome
  # so a resolver hard-coded to one spelling silently breaks on the other.
  # We drive the REAL resolver (bin/serve --check) against fixture bundles for
  # every known layout via CHROME_DEVTOOLS_MCP_BROWSERS — no nix build, no
  # network, no version drift. The buggy `chrome-linux64`-only glob fails the
  # `chrome-linux` case below (reproducing #3); the `chrome-linux*` fix passes.
  glob-resolution:
    name: bin/serve resolves Chrome across bundle layouts (issue #3)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Resolve Chrome for every known bundle layout
        run: |
          set -uo pipefail
          serve=.apm/skills/nix-chrome-devtools-mcp/bin/serve

          # Build a fixture bundle whose Chrome lives at $1, mark it executable,
          # and assert `bin/serve --check` resolves exactly that path.
          assert_resolves() {
            local label=$1 rel=$2
            local root chrome
            root=$(mktemp -d)
            chrome="$root/$rel"
            mkdir -p "$(dirname "$chrome")"
            : > "$chrome"; chmod +x "$chrome"
            local got
            if ! got=$(CHROME_DEVTOOLS_MCP_BROWSERS="$root" "$serve" --check); then
              echo "::error::[$label] bin/serve could not resolve Chrome at $rel — issue #3 reproduced"
              return 1
            fi
            if [[ "$got" != "$chrome" ]]; then
              echo "::error::[$label] resolved '$got', expected '$chrome'"
              return 1
            fi
            echo "OK [$label]: resolved $rel"
          }

          rc=0
          assert_resolves "linux (1.56.x)"  "chromium-1194/chrome-linux/chrome"   || rc=1
          assert_resolves "linux (1.60.x)"  "chromium-1223/chrome-linux64/chrome" || rc=1
          assert_resolves "macOS"           "chromium-1194/chrome-mac-x64/Google Chrome for Testing.app/Contents/MacOS/Google Chrome for Testing" || rc=1

          # Negative: an empty bundle must fail with the documented error.
          empty=$(mktemp -d)
          err=$(mktemp)
          if CHROME_DEVTOOLS_MCP_BROWSERS="$empty" "$serve" --check >/dev/null 2>"$err"; then
            echo "::error::[empty] expected failure, but resolution succeeded"; rc=1
          elif ! grep -q "no Chrome binary found" "$err"; then
            echo "::error::[empty] missing the documented 'no Chrome binary found' error"; rc=1
          else
            echo "OK [empty]: failed with the documented error"
          fi

          exit $rc

  # Integration smoke test: drive the resolver against whatever Chrome the
  # current nixpkgs actually ships, end to end (real nix build).
  live-nixpkgs:
    name: bin/serve resolves Chrome from live nixpkgs
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Install Nix
        uses: cachix/install-nix-action@v31
        with:
          extra_nix_config: |
            experimental-features = nix-command flakes

      - name: Resolve Chrome from nixpkgs#playwright-driver.browsers
        env:
          NIXPKGS_FLAKE: github:NixOS/nixpkgs/nixpkgs-unstable
        run: |
          set -uo pipefail
          serve=.apm/skills/nix-chrome-devtools-mcp/bin/serve
          echo "playwright-driver: $(nix eval --raw "$NIXPKGS_FLAKE#playwright-driver.version")"
          if ! chrome=$("$serve" --check); then
            echo "::error::bin/serve could not resolve Chrome from live nixpkgs"
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "Resolved Chrome: $chrome"
          [[ -x "$chrome" ]] || { echo "::error::not executable: $chrome"; exit 1; }
          echo "OK: Chrome resolved and executable"

# nix-chrome-devtools-mcp

One-click setup for the [Chrome DevTools MCP server](https://github.com/ChromeDevTools/chrome-devtools-mcp) in any Nix-based project. Delivered as an [APM](https://microsoft.github.io/apm/) package: add a single line to your project's [`apm.yml`](https://microsoft.github.io/apm/reference/manifest-schema/) and `apm install` does the rest — Chrome (Playwright's bundled Chrome-for-Testing) and Node.js resolve through Nix; the MCP server gets wired into every supported harness's runtime config (Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, …). No devshell to author, no flake to compose. The `nixpkgs` source is overridable per process or system-wide.

See [introductory blog post](https://kolu.dev/blog/nix-chrome-devtools-mcp/).

## Usage

Add to your project's [`apm.yml`](https://microsoft.github.io/apm/reference/manifest-schema/):

```yaml
dependencies:
  apm:
    - juspay/nix-chrome-devtools-mcp
```

`apm install` aggregates the MCP entry from this package's `apm.yml` into your runtime configs (`.mcp.json`, `.codex/config.toml`, `opencode.json`).

## Requirements

Nix — see [nixos.asia/en/install](https://nixos.asia/en/install). Flakes must be enabled (`experimental-features = nix-command flakes`).

## Overrides

The launcher reads two env vars:

| Var | Default | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `NIXPKGS_FLAKE` | `nixpkgs` | flake-ref used to resolve `playwright-driver.browsers` and `nodejs`. Examples: `github:NixOS/nixpkgs/<rev>`, `path:/abs/path/to/local/nixpkgs`. |
| `CHROME_DEVTOOLS_MCP_VERSION` | `latest` | npm dist-tag or version of `chrome-devtools-mcp` to install via `npx -y`. Pin to a specific version (e.g. `0.26.0`) when you need reproducibility. |

System-wide overrides also work:

- `nix registry pin nixpkgs github:NixOS/nixpkgs/<rev>` (replaces the default `nixpkgs` registry alias).
- Declare an overriding `mcp:` entry for `chrome-devtools` in the consumer's root `apm.yml` (root deps win APM's name-first dedupe).

## Screencast (video) recording

The launcher runs the server with `--experimentalScreencast=true` and puts
`ffmpeg` on its `PATH` (resolved through Nix, same as Chrome and Node), so the
`screencast_start` / `screencast_stop` tools are available out of the box. They
record the selected page to an `.mp4`/`.webm` file via Puppeteer's
`page.screencast()`, which shells out to ffmpeg — no host ffmpeg install needed.

## Chrome version compatibility

`chrome-devtools-mcp` is always pulled at `@latest` via `npx`. Each release transitively pins a Puppeteer version that expects a specific Chrome-for-Testing milestone; nixpkgs' `playwright-driver.browsers` provides a Chrome that may run a few major versions behind. CDP is largely backward-compatible, so the core operations (`navigate`, `evaluate`, `take_snapshot`, network/console inspection, screenshots) work, but Lighthouse-driven tooling (`performance_*` insights) is the most version-sensitive piece. If a `chrome-devtools-mcp` release breaks against your nixpkgs Chrome, override `NIXPKGS_FLAKE` to a newer nixpkgs revision whose Playwright Chrome matches Puppeteer's expected milestone.

Apache 2.0 — see [`LICENSE`](./LICENSE).

# nix-chrome-devtools-mcp

Drop-in launcher for the [Chrome DevTools MCP server](https://github.com/ChromeDevTools/chrome-devtools-mcp). Self-contained — `bin/serve` resolves all inputs via `nix build` / `nix shell`.

Full docs in the [repo README](https://github.com/juspay/nix-chrome-devtools-mcp/blob/main/README.md).

This skill primitive exists for APM's deployment convention — it ensures `bin/serve` lands at `.agents/skills/nix-chrome-devtools-mcp/bin/serve` in the consumer's working tree (per APM's [skills convergence](https://microsoft.github.io/apm/reference/targets-matrix/#skills-convergence) path), which keeps the launcher available even before `apm install` runs on a fresh clone. The package is mechanically a "skill" in APM's primitive vocabulary; semantically it's a tool.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Launch chrome-devtools-mcp using a Chrome-for-Testing binary resolved via
# Nix. Self-contained — no surrounding devshell required. Requires flakes
# (`experimental-features = nix-command flakes` in nix.conf).
#
# Override knobs (env vars):
#   NIXPKGS_FLAKE                 — flake-ref for nixpkgs (default: `nixpkgs`)
#   CHROME_DEVTOOLS_MCP_VERSION   — npm version of chrome-devtools-mcp
#                                   (default: `latest`)
#   CHROME_DEVTOOLS_MCP_BROWSERS  — path to an existing Playwright browser
#                                   bundle; skips the nix build (offline use,
#                                   and CI fixtures that exercise the resolver).
#
# Flags:
#   --check   resolve the Chrome binary, print its path, and exit (0 on
#             success, 1 if none found) — without launching the MCP server.
#             Used by CI; also handy for "which Chrome will this use?".

set -euo pipefail
shopt -s nullglob

nixpkgs="${NIXPKGS_FLAKE:-nixpkgs}"
mcp_version="${CHROME_DEVTOOLS_MCP_VERSION:-latest}"

browsers="${CHROME_DEVTOOLS_MCP_BROWSERS:-$(nix build --no-link --print-out-paths "${nixpkgs}#playwright-driver.browsers")}"

chrome=""
# chrome-linux* matches both spellings nixpkgs/playwright have shipped:
# chrome-linux64 (e.g. playwright-driver 1.60.0) and chrome-linux (1.56.1).
for c in \
    "$browsers"/chromium-*/chrome-linux*/chrome \
    "$browsers"/chromium-*/chrome-mac-*/"Google Chrome for Testing.app"/Contents/MacOS/"Google Chrome for Testing"; do
    if [[ -x "$c" ]]; then
        chrome="$c"
        break
    fi
done

if [[ -z "$chrome" ]]; then
    echo "nix-chrome-devtools-mcp: no Chrome binary found under $browsers" >&2
    exit 1
fi

# --check: report the resolved Chrome path and exit, without starting the MCP
# server. Lets CI assert detection works (issue #3) and gives users a quick
# "which Chrome will this use?".
if [[ "${1:-}" == "--check" ]]; then
    echo "$chrome"
    exit 0
fi

# ffmpeg is on PATH so chrome-devtools-mcp's experimental screencast tools
# (screencast_start / screencast_stop) can record page video — Puppeteer's
# page.screencast() shells out to ffmpeg. Without --experimentalScreencast
# the tools stay hidden; without ffmpeg they error at record time.
exec nix shell "${nixpkgs}#nodejs" "${nixpkgs}#ffmpeg" --command \
    npx -y "chrome-devtools-mcp@${mcp_version}" \
    --headless=true \
    --isolated=true \
    --experimentalScreencast=true \
    --executable-path="$chrome"

name: nix-chrome-devtools-mcp
version: 0.1.0
description: chrome-devtools-mcp launcher — a single bash launcher that resolves Playwright's bundled Chrome-for-Testing and Node.js directly through Nix. No devshell required.
type: hybrid

# Canonical MCP server entry for this package. APM aggregates this into
# the consumer's runtime configs via MCPIntegrator.collect_transitive
# (apm-cli src/apm_cli/integration/mcp_integrator.py:65) — depth-1 direct
# deps auto-trust self-defined servers.
dependencies:
  mcp:
    - name: chrome-devtools
      registry: false
      transport: stdio
      # `.agents/skills/<name>/` is APM's converged cross-tool skill deploy
      # path. The launcher is shipped as a skill primitive so the file is
      # deployed to (and tracked in) the consumer's working tree, which keeps
      # the MCP server bootable even before `apm install` runs on a fresh
      # clone (apm_modules/ is conventionally git-ignored).
      # https://microsoft.github.io/apm/reference/targets-matrix/#skills-convergence
      command: .agents/skills/nix-chrome-devtools-mcp/bin/serve
